transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-05
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 46m
Attendees: Alice Park (Redwood AE), Diego Ramos (Redwood SE), Maya Singh (Redwood CSM), Samir Patel (Orchard Eng), Laura Chen (Orchard ML Eng), Ravi Desai (Orchard Infra), Tess (Orchard SRE)

Summary (auto): quick wins from prefix normalization, still room on KV hit rate, eviction policy change proposed, next step 24h warmup run and share playbook + logs.

[00:00] Alice Park: hey everyone thanks for joining — kicking off, quick agenda — results from last week, eviction proposal, warmup plan, next steps
[00:18] Samir Patel: thanks alice, yep we ran the prefix normalization patch, so we saw some lift but it's noisy, we had like a bump from 18% up to about 39% KV hit but then tails go down during peak, um not sure if it's persistence or prompts changing
[00:36] Diego Ramos: yeah that aligns with what we saw in the sampling — prefix canonicalization helped dedupe about 14% of keys, so immediate wins but depends on prompt churn and session resets
[00:50] Laura Chen: one thing — our frontend often injects subtle user metadata that breaks prefix matching, so even normalized tokens look different — is there a way to do fuzzy key mapping or hashing at canonicalization time?
[01:12] Diego Ramos: we can add a normalization layer that strips low-value tokens and canonicalizes timestamps, ids; fuzzy mapping is possible but increases false positives — tradeoff on accuracy vs hit rate there
[01:35] Ravi Desai: also the eviction is very aggressive on our pods, we set low mem thresholds; so even if you get cache entries they get evicted before next request under bursty traffic, that's probably why tails drop
[01:52] Tess: agreed, we saw cache churn when a spike happened Thursday, a bunch of sessions got evicted and hit rate collapsed to single digits for 10 minutes
[02:07] Alice Park: ok so two levers: better canonicalization to increase prefix reuse and softer eviction policy / warmup to reduce churn — Diego, you proposed an LRU+TTL hybrid last week? can you summarize the change?
[02:22] Diego Ramos: sure — suggestion is a small TTL (120s) for short-lived prefixes plus an LRU weight based on recency and route importance; essentially high-value routes get heavier weight so they are less likely to be evicted under pressure. We also propose a transient prefetch for anticipated next-turn tokens for sessions that hit a threshold.
[02:48] Samir Patel: is that something we can tune live or need image deploy?
[02:55] Diego Ramos: config toggle for eviction parameters, no rebuild. Prefetch requires a small sidecar job to enqueue predicted prefixes into the KV store — it's optional for this pilot but easy to run as experiment.
[03:10] Laura Chen: the sidecar idea sounds ok but we worry about extra token cost from prefetching — how do you estimate net savings?
[03:21] Diego Ramos: we use a cost model: incremental tokens from prefetch minus avoided model calls due to hit. In our sim with Orchard's sample traffic, prefetch paid off for routes with >0.6 probability of next-turn reuse and mean latency sensitivity. We'll run a 24h A/B to confirm.
[03:39] Alice Park: quick question for Samir — what are your SLA targets if you moved to Dedicated? latency p50/p95 and cost band?
[03:49] Samir Patel: p50 < 120ms, p95 < 520ms, cost willing to be higher for reliability but need predictability — so Dedicated looks attractive if deltas are within our budget.
[04:05] Maya Singh: note — Alice will share a delta pricing spreadsheet for Dedicated vs Hosted with burst allowances and prepay options.
[04:14] [05:00] Speaker 2: (crosstalk) small side note — security ask from compliance: we need KMS integration details and audit log retention — have those docs?
[05:12] Alice Park: yes sent initial security packet last month, will attach more detailed KMS/HSM and audit-log retention docs to this thread — action item for me
[05:28] Tess: also SSO mapping for RBAC — we need sample roles and SCIM attributes, can Redwood share a template?
[05:38] Maya Singh: yes we'll share the SAML/SCIM mapping template.
[05:45] [08:15] Samir Patel: back to cache numbers — can you explain why prefix normalization gives such a broad swing in hit? I mean 18 to 39 seems high but then why 39 to 42 sometimes?
[08:33] Diego Ramos: it's because of a small number of high-volume prefixes — once you canonicalize them you grab a large fraction of requests, but a long tail of low-volume prefixes remains where normalization has less impact. Also session fragmentation and tokenization differences cause variance.
[08:56] Laura Chen: we're also seeing different seq len distributions across routes — some routes are 32-64 tokens, others are 512 — cache effectiveness differs by sequence length, right?
[09:06] Diego Ramos: yes, shorter interactions benefit more from prefix reuse. Long generative sessions have less reuse per token. We'll include per-route seq len histograms in the spreadsheet.
[09:24] Alice Park: ok action: Diego will run a 24h warmup/expt with new eviction params — what metrics do we want back?
[09:33] Samir Patel: per-route KV hit rate, per-route tail latency, eviction churn rate, prefetch false positive rate, cost delta per 1M requests
[09:43] Diego Ramos: adding: prefix reuse ratio, session-affinity violations, number of evictions per minute per pod
[09:50] Alice Park: perfect. Also Samir please give sample production traffic; we need realistic distributions for the sim.
[10:00] [11:12] Laura Chen: a question — is there a recommended way to canonicalize user-supplied content without losing semantics? we tried stripping user ids but that changed answers in some cases
[11:26] Diego Ramos: two approaches: conservative canonicalization (strip only clearly noise tokens like timestamps) vs aggressive (hashing numeric ids then treat as same). Conservative keeps semantics but lower hit; aggressive can boost hit but needs eval to check regression. We'll include eval tests in playbook.
[11:45] Samir Patel: could we add a regression alert if canonicalization drops ROUGE/BLEU or a selected metric?
[11:55] Alice Park: yes Redwood Optimize can hook regressions to prompt sets; we can configure a gate that fails a rollout if quality drops beyond threshold. Action item: include a small eval set for Orchard in the playbook.
[12:12] Maya Singh: I'll help onboard the eval harness and set thresholds with the ML team.
[12:22] [14:00] Tess: about warmup — we prefer background prefetch vs on-demand to avoid spikes, but background runs need to respect rate limits and be idempotent — any suggestions?
[14:12] Diego Ramos: recommended: stagger warmup tasks, limit per-second prefetch per pod, and only prefetch top-k prefixes per session. Also include adaptive backoff if you're seeing eviction storms.
[14:30] Alice Park: noted. Diego will provide a runbook with config knobs.
[14:40] [18:40] Laura Chen: curious — any nuance on cache keys for function/tool-calling or structured outputs? we sometimes have JSON shapes that vary order and break keys
[18:58] Diego Ramos: yes, need canonical JSON canonicalization (sort keys, remove whitespace) and stable serialization for structured outputs. We'll include canonicalizers for common payload types.
[19:20] [20:00] Samir Patel: can Redwood's runtime do prefix-aware routing so that hot prefixes get pinned to certain pods to improve locality?
[20:11] Diego Ramos: yes, session affinity and prefix steering can be used; downside is less load balancing — tradeoffs to discuss. For pilot we recommend soft steering (preferential routing with fallback).
[20:33] Alice Park: quick parity check: do any of you anticipate compliance or data residency blockers for using Hosted for pilot?
[20:42] Ravi Desai: not for pilot; final production we may need VPC/private deployment in EU region for data residency.
[20:52] Alice Park: ok we'll note that as decision criteria.
[21:10] [25:00] Diego Ramos: summary of proposed experiment: 1) enable prefix canonicalization + conservative canonicalizer, 2) change eviction to LRU+TTL (baseline TTL 120s), 3) run 24h warmup with staggered prefetch for top-3 prefixes per session, 4) collect per-route metrics and logs and share spreadsheet.
[25:34] Samir Patel: sounds good — what about the rollback plan if quality regression is detected?
[25:42] Diego Ramos: rollback is config flip for canonicalizer + eviction params; data in KV will gradually decay but immediate effect is reversed. We'll keep canary runs on 10% of traffic first.
[26:02] Alice Park: can we run the 24h on a canary subset first? say 10% traffic to measure?
[26:10] Diego Ramos: yes recommended. We'll do 10% canary for 4h, then ramp to 100% for the 24h full run if metrics look good.
[26:25] [30:40] Laura Chen: metrics threshold examples for go/no-go?
[30:48] Maya Singh: propose: KV hit rate increase >= +10pp net, p95 latency change <= +5%, quality regression <= 1% on sample eval metric. If these aren't met, don't roll to prod.
[31:04] Samir Patel: ok that sounds reasonable.
[31:12] Alice Park: security: Alice will re-share KMS and audit docs and Maya will send SCIM mapping template.
[31:25] [35:00] Tess: one more infra ask — we need hints about expected memory footprint of the extra prefetch entries per pod so we can size memory headroom
[35:11] Diego Ramos: we'll estimate based on average prefix size; preliminary is ~30-50MB per pod for top-k prefetch defaults. We'll put numbers in the playbook and runbook.
[35:26] Ravi Desai: that helps for capacity planning. If Dedicated, we can reserve instance types with more memory to reduce eviction.
[35:40] Alice Park: ok the timeline — Diego starts canary this week, full 24h by Mon 12/7, Diego shares logs by 12/10, Orchard to decide Dedicated by 12/20. Anyone opposed?
[35:56] Samir Patel: sounds good
[36:02] Laura Chen: good
[36:10] [40:00] Alice Park: final recap: Diego runs canary -> then 24h; Redwood shares cache-playbook + pricing delta + security templates; Orchard provides traffic samples and confirms SLA. Meeting closed, will send notes.
[40:28] Maya Singh: I'll create follow-up in calendar for 12/18 decision meeting.
[40:40] [45:30] (recording ends)
